subject: Vocabulary
description: Greek GEO (earth) and Latin TERR (earth, land) roots — geography, geology, terrestrial, territory, subterranean, Mediterranean.

questions.stem: GEO root means 'earth'. GEOGRAPHY literally means:
questions.explanation: GEOGRAPHY — etymology GEO (earth, Greek) + GRAPHY (writing, drawing) = 'earth-writing' = description/study of Earth's physical features, climate, populations, resources. KEY GEO-WORDS (memorize): (1) GEOGRAPHY — description of Earth. (2) GEOLOGY — study of Earth's structure (rocks, minerals, plate tectonics). (3) GEOMETRY — 'earth-measure' (originally land surveying; now math of shapes). (4) GEOPHYSICS — physics of Earth. (5) GEOTHERMAL — Earth heat. (6) GEOPOLITICS — politics of geography. (7) GEOCHEMISTRY — chemistry of Earth materials. (8) GEOMORPHOLOGY — study of landforms. (9) GEOCENTRIC — Earth-centered (vs heliocentric, sun-centered). (10) GEODESY — measurement of Earth's shape. RELATED -GRAPHY words: (a) BIOGRAPHY (life-writing). (b) AUTOGRAPHY (self-writing — auto). (c) PHOTOGRAPHY (light-writing). (d) BIBLIOGRAPHY (book-listing). (e) CARTOGRAPHY (map-making, kart from Greek 'chartes' = paper). (f) DEMOGRAPHY (people-writing — demos). (g) ETHNOGRAPHY (culture-writing). (h) CALLIGRAPHY (beautiful writing — kalli = beautiful). (i) STENOGRAPHY (narrow/short writing — shorthand). UPSC: GEOGRAPHY OPTIONAL papers cover physical, human, regional geography, plus environmental geography in PT. PYQ FREQUENCY: GEO root vocab in SSC CGL, CAT, UPSC English 1-2× per cycle.

questions.explanation: TERRESTRIAL — etymology TERRA (earth, Latin) + -ESTRIAL = 'pertaining to Earth/land'. Used: (1) BIOLOGY — terrestrial animals (live on land vs aquatic, arboreal). Examples: lion, elephant, snake. (2) ASTRONOMY — TERRESTRIAL PLANETS (rocky, like Earth) — Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (the inner planets). Contrast: GAS GIANTS (Jupiter, Saturn) and ICE GIANTS (Uranus, Neptune). (3) BROADCASTING — terrestrial TV (over-the-air signals from ground antennas, vs satellite TV). EXTRATERRESTRIAL = 'beyond Earth' = space/aliens (movie 'E.T.' = extraterrestrial). TERRA WORD FAMILY: (1) TERRITORY — 'land area' (claimed/owned). (2) TERRAIN — 'physical features of land'. (3) TERRACE — 'flat raised platform'. (4) SUBTERRANEAN — 'below the earth' (underground; e.g., subterranean tunnel, subway). (5) MEDITERRANEAN — 'middle of the lands' (between Europe + Africa + Asia). (6) TERRACOTTA — 'baked earth' (clay pottery, e.g., terracotta army of Qin Shi Huang in China). (7) TERRAFORM — to alter a planet's environment to be Earth-like (sci-fi for Mars colonization). (8) INTERN, INTERMENT — burial in earth. (9) DISINTER — to dig up. PYQ FREQUENCY: TERR-related vocab in SSC CGL, CAT, UPSC English 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: MEDITERRANEAN — etymology MEDI (middle, Latin) + TERRA (earth, land) + -ANEAN = 'in the middle of the lands' or 'sea between lands'. The MEDITERRANEAN SEA is enclosed by Europe (north), Africa (south), Asia (east). KEY GEOGRAPHIC FACTS: ~2.5 million sq km; connected to: (1) ATLANTIC OCEAN via STRAIT OF GIBRALTAR (only ~14 km wide, separates Spain + Morocco). (2) BLACK SEA via TURKISH STRAITS (Bosphorus, Dardanelles). (3) RED SEA via SUEZ CANAL (since 1869). MEDITERRANEAN CLIMATE: dry hot summers, mild wet winters; supports olive, grape, citrus, fig — characteristic 'Mediterranean diet'. CIVILIZATIONS born here: Egyptian, Phoenician, Greek, Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman. RECENT EVENTS: refugee crises across Mediterranean from N. Africa to Europe. MED WORD FAMILY (root MEDI = middle, Latin): (1) MEDIATE — be in middle, settle dispute. (2) MEDIAN — middle value. (3) MEDIUM — middle/intermediate. (4) IMMEDIATE — without delay (without anything in middle). (5) INTERMEDIATE — in between. (6) MEDIOCRE — average (medium quality). MEDIEVAL is from a different root (medi + aevum, age) — middle ages. UPSC angle: Mediterranean climate type appears in geography PT — also climate-zone classification (Köppen system). PYQ FREQUENCY: Mediterranean concept in geography MCQ, etymology in CAT.

questions.explanation: SUBTERRANEAN — etymology SUB (under, Latin) + TERRA (earth) + -EAN = 'under the earth' = UNDERGROUND. EXAMPLES: (1) Subterranean RIVERS — flow underground (Mahanadi tributaries in some regions). (2) Subterranean PASSAGES — tunnels, escape routes (e.g., in ancient forts). (3) SUBWAY systems — subterranean trains (Delhi Metro has many underground sections; New York Subway, London Underground, Paris Metro, Moscow Metro famous worldwide). (4) Subterranean CAVES — Mawsmai (Meghalaya), Belum (Andhra), Borra (Andhra) caves in India. (5) Subterranean ECOSYSTEMS — unique cave-dwelling species (blind fish, salamanders adapted to dark). KEY 'SUB' words (root SUB = under): SUBMARINE (under sea), SUBTERRANEAN (under earth), SUBCONSCIOUS (below conscious thought), SUBSTANDARD (below standard), SUBSCRIBE (sign under), SUBJECT, SUBSIDIZE, SUBORDINATE. RELATED CONCEPTS: TROGLODYTE = cave-dweller; TROGLOBITES = species that live entirely in caves. UPSC angle: SUBTERRANEAN water resources (groundwater) — key for India's water security; aquifer depletion in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan; managed aquifer recharge as a UPSC GS-3 environment topic. CENTRAL GROUND WATER BOARD (CGWB) monitors. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'sub-' prefix vocab in SSC CGL, CAT 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: GEOTHERMAL — etymology GEO (earth) + THERMAL (heat) = 'earth-heat'. Energy harnessed from heat naturally produced inside Earth's mantle/core (radioactive decay + residual heat from Earth's formation 4.5 billion years ago). USES: (1) ELECTRICITY GENERATION — drilling wells to extract steam/hot water that drives turbines. Top countries: USA, Indonesia, Philippines, Turkey, New Zealand, Iceland, Italy. ICELAND gets ~25% of electricity + 90% of home heating from geothermal — sits on Mid-Atlantic Ridge. (2) DIRECT HEATING — homes (Iceland), greenhouses, fish farming, district heating (Boise, Idaho, USA — first geothermal heating system 1892). (3) GEOTHERMAL HEAT PUMPS — household heating/cooling using Earth as thermal reservoir (~10-15°C below surface year-round). INDIA POTENTIAL: 340+ identified hotspots including PUGA VALLEY (Ladakh), MANIKARAN (HP), TATTAPANI (Chhattisgarh), TAPTAPANI (Odisha). PUGA development project initiated 2024. ESTIMATED INDIAN POTENTIAL: ~10 GW (per GSI). VOLCANIC HOTSPOTS — Iceland, Japan, New Zealand have abundant geothermal due to plate tectonics. UPSC angle: geothermal under RENEWABLE ENERGY policy; Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE); Climate change mitigation (NDC commitments). PYQ FREQUENCY: geothermal in UPSC PT, NEET environment, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: TERRACOTTA — etymology TERRA (earth) + COTTA (cooked, Italian) = 'baked/cooked earth'. CLAY-BASED CERAMIC made by molding clay then firing at relatively low temperatures (~600-1000°C). NATURAL color: orange-brown-red (iron oxide content); after firing, retains color. USES historic + modern: (1) POTTERY — ancient civilizations everywhere; Indus Valley (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) had extensive terracotta. (2) ROOFING TILES (Mediterranean, Italian style; common in India). (3) ARCHITECTURAL ORNAMENT — facades, friezes. (4) SCULPTURE — TERRACOTTA WARRIORS of CHINA (Qin Shi Huang's tomb, ~210 BCE; ~8,000 life-sized warriors discovered 1974). (5) VESSELS — water pots ('matka' in Hindi) — keep water cool through evaporation. (6) DIYAS (oil lamps for Diwali). INDIA: Bishnupur (West Bengal) — UNESCO terracotta temples. Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Bengal — major centers of terracotta craftsmanship. ETYMOLOGY ITALIAN: 'terra' (earth) + 'cotta' (past participle of 'cuocere', to cook). PARALLEL WORDS: BISCOTTI (twice-cooked biscuits), COTTAGE (small heated dwelling — different etymology though). KEY: 'TERRA' appears in many Italian-origin English words about earth/land. UPSC ART & CULTURE: terracotta in CSE Mains has appeared in Indian-art questions. PYQ FREQUENCY: TERR vocab in CGL, IBPS PO, CAT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: GEODESIC, related to GEO root, means:
questions.explanation: GEODESIC — etymology GEO (earth) + DESIA (division, Greek) — relates to GEODESY (measurement of Earth's shape). KEY USES: (1) GEODESIC DOMES — by Buckminster Fuller (1950s); spherical structures built from triangles, very strong + light. Famous example: EPCOT's Spaceship Earth at Disney World, Florida. (2) GEODESIC PATHS — shortest line between two points on a curved surface (e.g., great circle on Earth's sphere). Airlines fly geodesic routes — appear curved on flat maps but are shortest in 3D space; classic example: Delhi to New York flight crosses near Arctic. (3) GENERAL RELATIVITY — spacetime is curved; objects travel on geodesics (shortest paths). PARALLEL CONCEPTS in MATH: (a) GEODESIC on flat plane = straight line. (b) On a sphere (e.g., Earth) = great circle (e.g., equator, meridians). (c) In Einstein's General Relativity = path through curved spacetime. KEY MEASUREMENTS: GEODESY → defines Earth's shape (oblate spheroid; equatorial radius ~6,378 km, polar ~6,357 km). GPS uses geodesy to compute positions. INDIA's SURVEY OF INDIA (founded 1767) — oldest scientific dept; conducts geodesic surveys for maps + boundaries. RELATED 'DESIA' words: rare; mostly geodesy and derivatives. PYQ FREQUENCY: rare-vocabulary like 'geodesic' in CAT, GRE, UPSC English-comprehension 1× per 2 cycles. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests advanced GEO-root knowledge.
